objectives: To systematically evaluate, by meta-analysis, the safety of hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in treating gastrointestinal malignancies, addressing a central clinical concern that often dictates its adoptability independent of efficacy considerations, and to provide evidence-based medical support for its clinical application.
inclusion_criteria: English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs); patients diagnosed with advanced gastric or colorectal cancer with peritoneal metastases; HIPEC as the experimental intervention; a non-HIPEC control group; and studies reporting relevant data on the incidence of adverse reactions or complications.
exclusion_criteria: Excluded were studies in patients without gastric or colorectal cancer; studies not using HIPEC; non-randomized controlled trials, case analyses, review articles, protocols, pilot studies, single-arm clinical trials, and multi-arm trials lacking a control group; and studies with incomplete outcome indicators, unobtainable data, or data that could not be converted.

selection_evidence: Results/Figure 1 report that 10 RCTs were included. Main Table 1 lists 10 study authors/years, and Supplementary Table 2 repeats the same 10 included trials: Rau B 2024, Yang XJ 2011, Quenet F 2021, Verwaal VJ 2003, Yu P 2023, Liu L 2022, Fan B 2021, Huang O 2015, Beeharry MK 2019, and Baratti D 2020. Matching those author/year entries to the numbered manuscript reference list yields Rau B 2024=8, Yang XJ 2011=9, Quenet F 2021=10, Verwaal VJ 2003=11, Yu P 2023=12, Liu L 2022=13, Fan B 2021=14, Huang O 2015=15, Beeharry MK 2019=16, and Baratti D 2020=17. These references are all literature citations; no website, dataset, or software references are included in refs 8-17.
notes: The article-in-press Table 1 shows broken citation placeholders ("Error: Reference source not found") instead of visible superscript reference numbers, so the selected ref numbers were reconstructed by exact author/year matching between Table 1/Supplementary Table 2 and the numbered reference list. The stated eligibility criteria require peritoneal metastases, but Results 2.3.1 says 3 included trials were adjuvant/prophylactic without documented peritoneal metastases at surgery.
